signals.text: Charging and Remissions Policy Jack Tizard School recognises the valuable contribution that the wide range of additional activities, including trips and residential experiences, can make toward our pupils’ personal and social education.

There will be a balance of group and individual work and pupils experience a range of activities including sensory stories, music, sensory art, Rebound Therapy, Intensive Interaction and hydrotherapy.

Through topic work, outings and other school activities we provide our pupils with a wide range of experiences, giving them a chance to start to understand their world and to begin forming preferences and opinions.

In particular, it seeks to enhance the wellbeing of students, local disabled children and young people, and their families by extending the use of the school's state-of-the-art hydrotherapy pool after school, at the weekends and during school holidays.

The School is literally next door to Queens Park Rangers Football Club and fifteen minutes walk from Westfield Shopping Centre and the BBC; it has excellent transport links, including Wood Lane and White City tube stations a ten minute walk away.

School Life
What People Say
Jack Tizard is an outstanding school for pupils aged 2 to 19 years with a range of severe learning difficulties (SLD) and profound and multiple learning difficulties (PMLD).
Jack Tizard is a happy, friendly school where pupils are encouraged and supported to learn and achieve, through a highly personalised curriculum. Each child and young person within the school is treated as a unique individual and the multi-disciplinary approach to learning provides the opportunities for them to reach their full potential.
The Jack Tizard staff team are proud of the learning environment; one that is caring, supportive, stimulating, enjoyable, age respectful and challenging. We work in close partnership with parents, staff, pupils and the wider community to support learning and achievement.
Jack Tizard School is committed to the positive social inclusion of all our pupils through person centred approaches to learning, communication, independence and community links.
Within Jack Tizard School we promote an ethos of respect for all regardless of gender, race, sexuality, social background, ability, nationality or religion. The contribution of every individual is valued equally.
What People Say
"I believe Jack Tizard School are truly unique. They take person centred practice to the next level and constantly amaze me with their sector leading creative approaches to inclusive education. They strive relentlessly to ensure each young person is engaged thoughtfully in every aspect of school life; with a keenness that is unmatched, to see each person's unique progression. We love working with Jack Tizard who constantly push us to be the best we can be"
Vicki Hawkins, Co-Director, BLINK Dance Theatre
"One of the many things I love about Jack Tizard (and one of the reasons I keep coming back for more, after nearly 20 years) is the shared sense of purpose amongst the students, the parents, the classroom teams, the teachers, the therapy and health teams, the admin and management staff and visiting others, towards overcoming some of more challenging barriers to learning experienced anywhere, with healthy doses of creativity, persistence, kindness, humour and optimism, so those amazing moments - when new communication or mobility or learning milestones are met - keep happening. That’s a mighty long sentence… but there’s so much to say!"
Tom Lloyd Senior Educational Psychologist H&F EPS
"When you go to Jack Tizard School you feel such a positive atmosphere.
It was a pleasure to work with all staff but also with our amazing pupils. There are many things (I cannot choose just one). I thoroughly enjoyed working with my co-workers and SLT. It has been always a friendly and supportive atmosphere where you feel so motivated to go to work every day. But also, to see our pupils progress gave me that motivation to do more and more. I specifically liked about my role at JT that everyone in the school shared the same vision and was dedicated to support our pupils and their families. This created a strong work environment where we were all willing to support each other and build a team."

About Us
We are a day school for pupils aged 2-19 years with a range of severe learning difficulties (SLD) including profound and multiple learning difficulties (PMLD). We serve the community of Hammersmith and Fulham and accept pupils from a range of other boroughs. Pupils attending Jack Tizard School either have a statement of special educational needs and receive annual reviews, or they attend on an assessment placement. The school population consists of pupils from a range of social, cultural and ethnic backgrounds.
The school's goal is to enable each pupil to develop his or her full potential. A broad and balanced curriculum is provided that is differentiated to meet individual needs and which enables access to the National Curriculum. The ethos of the school is founded on the principle of respect for all regardless of gender, race, sexuality, social background, ability, nationality or religion. The contribution of every individual is valued equally. The school promotes the positive social inclusion of all its pupils by fostering community links and by raising the profile of the school within the borough of Hammersmith and Fulham.
Head Teacher: Francesca Smith

Who was Jack Tizard
Psychologist Jack Tizard was a New Zealander who spent most of his professional life in England.

Curriculum Aims
At Jack Tizard School, we believe that each pupil has the right to learn within an environment that is personalised, caring, supportive, stimulating, enjoyable, age respectful and challenging.
Our teaching and learning opportunities are woven into the whole school day. For example, snack time provides opportunities to work on communication, making choices, being independent. By learning in ‘real life’ contexts, our pupils are supported to generalise their skills into other settings such as home, going out with their families etc.At Jack Tizard the Primary Department covers EYFS and Key Stage One and Two. The Secondary Department covers Key Stage Three and the Post 16 Curriculum. Our curriculum pathways run through all phases of learning and allow for approaches specific to individual needs - PMLD, ASD and Sensory, and SLD. With each pathway covering skills, knowledge and understanding across a range of areas of learning, pupils can move between the pathways at any point during their school career. We focus on the stage of learning whilst respecting the child’s chronological age, providing opportunities which offer breadth, support and challenge and fun!
Makes learning fun!

Special educational needs
A pupil is defined as having special educational needs (SEN) if they have a learning difficulty or disability which requires special educational provision to be made for them. Special educational needs provision and the 'local offer' Changes implemented in September 2014 as a result of the Children and Families Act means that SEN services are now offered as part of a joined up service which brings together education, health and social care services to ensure that the support your child receives is joined up and that the outcomes that you and your child want to achieve are always at the centre of that help and support. This is known nationally as the 'local offer'.

Working at Jack Tizard School
Jack Tizard is a friendly, supportive, purpose-built all age school for pupils with severe learning difficulties, located in the north of the London Borough of Hammersmith & Fulham. The School is literally next door to Queens Park Rangers Football Club and fifteen minutes walk from Westfield Shopping Centre and the BBC; it has excellent transport links, including Wood Lane and White City tube stations a ten minute walk away.
Working at Jack Tizard school is a rewarding career choice. Whatever post you are in, you are part of a valuable team of professionals that believe in working together and supporting each other to obtain the best possible results for each and every child. Within the school we have an increasing number of pupils with profound and multiple learning difficulties and complex needs. We are an outward looking community school with an innovative, well developed curriculum and highly regarded outreach and inclusion service.
We regularly recruit friendly, enthusiastic, hard working and reliable people to work as Teaching Assistants, as part of a team under the direction of our class teachers. To work at Jack Tizard School, you need good communication skills and relate well to children. You must be willing to work flexibly across the school as required, and whilst experience with special needs children is desirable, it is not essential as we offer a good induction programme. A positive attitude is more important along with a sense of humour!
Jack Tizard is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and staff share this commitment. An enhanced DBS disclosure is required for successful appointees in accordance with Safeguarding Children and Safer Recruitment in Education legislation.

SEND Policy Report
Jack Tizard is a maintained special school in Hammersmith and Fulham for children with complex physical, health and learning difficulties. We believe that all pupils are entitled to a safe, supportive and stimulating environment in which they are happy, healthy and enabled, and are encouraged to achieve as individuals. Jack Tizard School offers a positive, enjoyable, life-enhancing education, and provides a range of opportunities for the development of each pupil.

Therapy
At Jack Tizard School, therapy is integrated into every pupil's day. We believe that incorporating therapy principles into a pupil's daily life is the best way to help them to achieve his/her potential. Our main aim within Jack Tizard School, is to help children and young people to learn how to advocate for themselves and be as independent as possible.The therapy team consists of Speech and Language Therapists, Physiotherapists and Occupational Therapists. We often work together to make the best of everyone's expertise, and ensure we are all working towards the same goals. All of the therapists work closely with the teachers and teaching assistants to ensure that the recommended activities or exercises for specific pupils are integrated into the school setting.The Jack Tizard School therapists' communicate with parents/carers regularly and we welcome their input. Parents, carers and other professionals can contact us at school for a chat or to ask us to see a particular child or young person. This could be via a phone call, email, spoken in person, in a written letter/note, via the home-school communication book, or in the messages book in the therapy office at school. Physiotherapy
Hello and welcome to Physiotherapy at Jack Tizard school. The team based at Jack Tizard are members of the childrens physiotherapy team from Chelsea and Westminster NHS Trust. We are in a unique position of being able to bring the ethos of both Jack Tizard and the NHS together, working to provide the best possible physiotherapy input for the students at Jack Tizard.
Clinics
We are very lucky to have many speciality services come into our school to run their clinics on a regular basis throughout the year. By having these clinics based at our school, pupils miss out on less school time to attend appointments. Families often report that it is easier for them to travel to school clinics rather than to the hospitals, and usually, our pupils feel much more comfortable being seen at school than in an unfamiliar setting.Some of the clinics we offer at Jack Tizard School include:
Orthotics clinic
Orthopaedic clinic
Medical clinic
Dental clinic
